questions.question: Which state government started the 'Shantala Natya Sri Award' in 1995 in the field of classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shantala Natya Sri Award** was initiated by the **Karnataka State Government** in **1995**.
 
• This award is dedicated to the field of **classical dance** and is named after **Queen Shantala**, who was a renowned patron of art and culture.
 
• Queen Shantala was the wife of **King Vishnuvardhana** of the **Hoysala dynasty** and was known for her exceptional contributions to the promotion of art forms, especially dance.
 
• The award aims to honor and recognize excellence in the domain of **Indian classical dance**, which includes forms like **Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, and Odissi**.
 
• Karnataka has a rich cultural heritage and a strong connection to classical art forms, making it an ideal state to institute such an award.
 
• The **Shantala Natya Sri Award** is one of the most prestigious recognitions in the field of dance and serves as a motivation for artists to preserve and promote traditional Indian dance forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Assam**__

 __
 
• **Assam** is known for its traditional dance forms like **Bihu** and **Sattriya** (one of the eight classical dance forms of India).
 
• It is a northeastern state of India with a rich tradition of art, culture, and music.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__
 __
 
• **Andhra Pradesh** is renowned for its classical dance form **Kuchipudi**, which originated in the state.
 
• The state has a long tradition of promoting classical arts and culture.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu** is the birthplace of **Bharatanatyam**, one of the oldest classical dance forms of India.
 
• It has a rich tradition of temple dances and classical music, especially associated with the temples of **Chidambaram and Thanjavur**.

questions.question: 'Roppi' is a popular folk dance from the state of __________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Roppi** is a traditional folk dance that originates from the state of **Arunachal Pradesh**, a state in northeastern India.
 
• This dance is primarily performed by the **Adi tribe**, one of the major tribal groups in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The dance is usually performed during **festivals, community celebrations, and cultural events**.
 
• It is characterized by its **graceful and rhythmic movements**, often accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the **drums and cymbals**.
 
• **Roppi** symbolizes **joy, harmony, and community spirit**, making it an essential part of the cultural heritage of the Adi tribe.
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is known for its **rich cultural diversity**, with several tribes contributing to its unique traditions and art forms.
 
• This state celebrates various festivals such as **Solung, Losar, and Dree**, during which traditional dances like **Roppi** are performed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kerala**__

 __
 
• Kerala is known for its famous classical and folk dances like **Mohiniyattam, Kathakali, Theyyam, and Thiruvathira.**
 
• The state is located in the **southern part of India**, known for its **backwaters, Ayurveda, and rich cultural heritage.**
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form that is performed exclusively by women and is deeply rooted in the **traditions of Kerala.**
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**__
 __
 
• Karnataka is famous for its folk dances such as **Dollu Kunitha, Yakshagana, and Veeragase.**
 
• The state is located in the **southwestern region of India** and is known for its **heritage sites and classical art forms.**
 
• **Yakshagana** is a unique dance-drama that combines **music, dance, and dialogue delivery** to narrate mythological stories.
 
 
 
• **Assam**__
 
 
• Assam is known for its famous dance forms like **Bihu, Sattriya, and Bagurumba.**
 
• **Bihu** is performed during the **Bihu festival**, which marks the Assamese New Year.
 
• Sattriya is one of the **classical dance forms of India** and has its origins in the **Vaishnavite monasteries** of Assam.

questions.question: How can a high fiscal deficit lead to crowding out in the economy?

options.text: By enhancing the availability of credit for businesses
By reducing government borrowing and debt
By leading to higher interest rates and reduced private investment
By increasing private investment in the market

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**By leading to higher interest rates and reduced private investment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **high fiscal deficit** occurs when a government's total expenditure exceeds its total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• To finance a fiscal deficit, the government often resorts to **borrowing from the market**, which creates competition for available funds.
 
• This increased demand for funds in the market leads to a rise in **interest rates**, as lenders seek higher returns due to greater demand for capital.
 
• Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive for private businesses, discouraging **private investment** in the economy.
 
• The phenomenon where government borrowing "crowds out" private investment is called **crowding out.**
 
• This can lead to slower economic growth, as private investment is a key driver of innovation, employment, and productivity.
 
• The crowding-out effect is particularly significant in economies with **limited savings** and a smaller pool of financial resources.
 
• In contrast, if fiscal deficits are managed effectively and funds are channeled into productive investments, they can stimulate economic growth without significant crowding out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **By enhancing the availability of credit for businesses**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect because a high fiscal deficit typically reduces the availability of credit for private businesses rather than enhancing it, due to the government absorbing a significant share of the available funds.
 
• **Increased government borrowing** often leads to less credit being available for the private sector, exacerbating the crowding-out effect.
 
 
 
• **By reducing government borrowing and debt**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because a high fiscal deficit actually increases government borrowing and debt, not reduces it.
 
• **Fiscal deficit** is a measure of the shortfall between the government's income and expenditure, which is filled through borrowing.
 
 
 
• **By increasing private investment in the market**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because a high fiscal deficit generally discourages private investment due to the crowding-out effect caused by higher interest rates.
 
• Private businesses face **higher borrowing costs**, making it less attractive to invest in new projects.
 
 
 
• **Key Points for Exams**__
 
 
• **Crowding out**: A situation where increased government borrowing leads to reduced private sector investment.
 
• **Interest rates**: A crucial factor influenced by government borrowing and fiscal policy.
 
• **Fiscal deficit**: The difference between the government's expenditure and revenue, excluding borrowings.

questions.question: The Indian badminton team won the Thomas Cup title for the first time in 2022 with a spectacular victory over the team of _________.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Lanthanides along with which two elements are sometimes called 'rare earth elements'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Yttrium and Scandium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lanthanides** along with **Yttrium** and **Scandium** are often referred to as **'rare earth elements'**.
 
• Rare earth elements are a group of **17 chemically similar elements**, including the 15 lanthanides plus **Yttrium** and **Scandium**.
 
• **Yttrium** and **Scandium** are grouped with lanthanides because of their similar **chemical properties** and occurrence in the same mineral deposits.
 
• These elements are critical for applications in **electronics, renewable energy technologies, aerospace, and defense industries**.
 
• Examples of their uses include **magnets, phosphors, batteries, and catalysts**.
 
• Rare earth elements are typically found in **low concentrations in the Earth's crust**, making their extraction challenging and contributing to the term "rare."
 
• The **geopolitical importance** of rare earth elements is significant due to their role in high-tech applications and limited global production centers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vanadium and Niobium**__

 __
 
• **Vanadium** is a transition metal used primarily in **steel alloys** to improve hardness and durability.
 
• **Niobium** is used in **superconducting materials** and specialized steel alloys for aerospace and construction industries.
 
• These elements are not classified as rare earth elements due to their **distinct chemical and physical properties**.
 
 
 
• **Ruthenium and Zirconium**__
 __
 
• **Ruthenium** is a member of the platinum group metals and is used in **electronics, catalysts, and jewelry.**
 
• **Zirconium** is utilized for **nuclear reactors, ceramics, and corrosion-resistant applications.**
 
• These elements are not related to rare earth elements due to their differing **classification and occurrence.**
 
 
 
• **Molybdenum and Palladium**__
 
 
• **Molybdenum** is a transition metal known for its use in **steel alloys, electronics, and catalysts.**
 
• **Palladium**, a platinum group metal, is used in **automotive catalytic converters, electronics, and jewelry.**
 
• These elements have distinct applications and are not part of the rare earth elements group.

questions.question: Which Indian leader known as the 'Frontier Gandhi'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** was popularly known as the '**Frontier Gandhi**' due to his close association with Mahatma Gandhi and his commitment to the principles of **non-violence** and **peace.**
 
• He was a prominent **freedom fighter** and leader from the **North-West Frontier Province (now in Pakistan).**
 
• He founded the **Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God)** movement, which was dedicated to the principles of **non-violence** and the **upliftment of society.**
 
• He was the first non-Indian to be awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian honor, in **1987**.
 
• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a staunch advocate of **Hindu-Muslim unity** and worked tirelessly to bridge communal divides during the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• Due to his efforts in the region, he is remembered as a symbol of **peace, resilience, and unity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Liaquat Ali Khan**__

 __
 
• **Liaquat Ali Khan** was the first **Prime Minister of Pakistan** after the partition of India in **1947**.
 
• He played a key role in the creation of Pakistan and was a close associate of **Mohammed Ali Jinnah**.
 
• He is known for his contributions to Pakistan’s early political and economic policies.
 
 
 
• **Shaukat Ali**__
 __
 
• **Shaukat Ali** was a prominent leader of the **Khilafat Movement** in India, which aimed to preserve the authority of the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• He was the elder brother of **Mohammad Ali Jauhar** and worked for the unity of Muslims in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He was known for his strong support of the **Muslim League** and its objectives.
 
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**__
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was an eminent **freedom fighter**, scholar, and the first **Education Minister of independent India.**
 
• He was a proponent of **Hindu-Muslim unity** and was a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress.**
 
• He played a significant role in the **Non-Cooperation Movement** and was a key figure in India’s independence struggle.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following about mitosis.

options.text: Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.
It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms.
The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mitosis is a type of **cell division** that results in two genetically identical daughter cells from a single parent cell.
 
• The daughter cells produced by mitosis have the **same number of chromosomes** as the parent cell, making them diploid.
 
• This process is essential for the **growth, repair, and maintenance** of tissues in multicellular organisms.
 
• Unlike meiosis, which results in daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes (haploid), mitosis maintains the **chromosome number** of the original cell.
 
• Mitosis consists of several phases: **Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase, and Cytokinesis**, ensuring accurate chromosome segregation and cell division.
 
• The incorrect statement suggests that mitosis results in daughter cells with half the chromosomes, which is characteristic of **meiosis**, not mitosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells**__

 __
 
• This is a correct statement as mitosis results in the formation of **two genetically identical daughter cells** from a single parent cell.
 
• It ensures that the daughter cells maintain the **same genetic makeup** as the parent cell.
 
 
 
• **It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms**__
 __
 
• Mitosis plays a crucial role in **growth, development, and repair** of tissues in multicellular organisms.
 
• It is vital for the replacement of damaged or dead cells, ensuring the proper functioning of tissues and organs.
 
 
 
• **Cells divide for growth**__
 
 
• Mitosis is a fundamental process for **cellular growth** and development, allowing organisms to increase in size.
 
• This division ensures that new cells are available for the expansion and maintenance of tissues.

questions.question: Which Mauryan archaeological site is associated with the remains of a wooden palisade?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bulandibagh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bulandibagh** is an archaeological site located in **Pataliputra, Bihar**.
 
• The site is associated with the remains of a **wooden palisade**, which is indicative of ancient fortifications and urban planning during the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• The wooden palisade remnants are crucial as they provide evidence of the **structural techniques** used during the Mauryan period.
 
• **Pataliputra**, the capital of the Mauryan Empire, was a highly advanced urban center known for its **fortified architecture.**
 
• The discovery of wooden palisades at Bulandibagh highlights the **strategic importance** of this site in protecting the city from invasions.
 
• The Mauryan archaeological remains at Bulandibagh include structures that reflect the **military and administrative organization** of the empire.
 
• The site provides valuable insights into the **engineering capabilities** and materials used during ancient times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhita**__

 __
 
• **Bhita** is an ancient archaeological site located near **Allahabad (Prayagraj), Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The site is known for its **Gupta period remains**, including sculptures, pottery, and terracotta objects.
 
• It reflects the cultural and economic significance of the region during ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Mathura**__
 __
 
• **Mathura** is a historically significant city located in **Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• It is famous for its **artistic and religious heritage**, especially during the Kushan period.
 
• Mathura is known for its **Buddhist and Jain sculptures**, along with Hindu religious artifacts.
 
 
 
• **Taxila**__
 
 
• **Taxila** is an ancient city located in present-day **Pakistan**.
 
• It was a major center of learning and culture during ancient times, particularly during the **Gandhara period.**
 
• Taxila is famous for its **monasteries, stupas, and ancient universities**.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Articles 12 to 35**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are provided under **Articles 12 to 35**.
 
• Fundamental Rights guarantee civil liberties to all citizens of India, ensuring equality, freedom, and justice.
 
• Key Fundamental Rights include:
 
 
• The **Right to Equality** (Articles 14-18).
 
• The **Right to Freedom** (Articles 19-22).
 
• The **Right against Exploitation** (Articles 23-24).
 
• The **Right to Freedom of Religion** (Articles 25-28).
 
• The **Cultural and Educational Rights** (Articles 29-30).
 
• The **Right to Constitutional Remedies** (Article 32).
 
 
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their Fundamental Rights are violated.
 
• The **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** have the power to enforce these rights through writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are inspired by the **United States Bill of Rights**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Articles 15 to 35**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **Articles 15 to 35** cover only a part of the Fundamental Rights.
 
• While some Fundamental Rights like the **Right to Equality** and **Right to Freedom** are included here, **Articles 12-14** are also essential for defining Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Articles 2 to 7**__
 __
 
• **Articles 2 to 7** are related to provisions regarding the **admission of new states** or **alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states**.
 
• These articles are not related to Fundamental Rights but to the organization of states in India.
 
 
 
• **Articles 10 to 40**__
 
 
• **Articles 10 to 40** do not exclusively deal with Fundamental Rights.
 
• They include provisions such as **citizenship** and **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).**
 
• **Directive Principles** (Articles 36-51) are non-justiciable guidelines to the State, unlike Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable.

questions.question: What was the central objective of planning in India?

options.text: To initiate a process of privatisation
To initiate a process of development

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To initiate a process of development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The central objective of planning in India was to initiate a process of **economic and social development**.
 
• After independence in 1947, India faced challenges such as **poverty, illiteracy, unemployment**, and a lack of infrastructure.
 
• Planning was introduced to ensure a **balanced growth** across different sectors of the economy.
 
• The government established the **Planning Commission** in 1950 to formulate and oversee the implementation of five-year plans aimed at achieving growth and development.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan (1951–1956) focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and energy** to improve food production and rural infrastructure.
 
• Subsequent plans aimed at reducing **regional disparities, promoting industrialization**, and improving the standard of living for citizens.
 
• The process of development included investments in **education, healthcare, transportation, energy**, and the establishment of industries.
 
• The planning system also emphasized **self-reliance** in food production and technology to reduce dependence on foreign aid.
 
• The objective was to create a framework for **sustainable economic growth** and social equity while addressing the country's long-term needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To initiate a process of privatization**__

 __
 
• Privatization refers to the **transfer of ownership** of public sector enterprises to private entities.
 
• While privatization became a key reform under the **Liberalization policy in 1991**, it was not the central objective of planning in India during the initial years post-independence.
 
• The early planning phases focused on building a strong public sector to drive growth and development.
 
 
 
• **To follow British culture**__
 __
 
• India aimed to break away from colonial influences and develop its own identity post-independence.
 
• The planning process was rooted in principles of **self-reliance** and aimed at addressing the specific needs of the Indian population.
 
• There was no objective to follow British culture as part of the planning process.
 
 
 
• **To initiate uniqueness**__
 
 
• While India's approach to planning was unique in its focus on a mixed economy, this was not explicitly stated as the central objective.
 
• The emphasis was on development rather than creating uniqueness.

questions.question: Chapchar Kut Festival, which is celebrated in anticipation of a golden harvest, is primarily a festival from __________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chapchar Kut** is the most celebrated and oldest festival of the state of **Mizoram**, India.
 
• It is celebrated in anticipation of a **golden harvest** and marks the end of the arduous task of jungle-clearing for jhum cultivation (shifting agriculture).
 
• The festival is observed in **March every year**, after the completion of the initial stage of farming known as “clearing of the forests.”
 
• The festival is marked by traditional **folk dances, music, and cultural performances**, showcasing the rich heritage of the Mizo community.
 
• People wear their traditional attire and participate in dances such as the **Cheraw dance**, also known as the bamboo dance.
 
• The festival promotes **unity, joy, and cultural preservation** among the Mizo people.
 
• Chapchar Kut is not just a religious or agricultural festival but also an opportunity for **social bonding and showcasing Mizo traditions** to the younger generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uttarakhand**__

 __
 
• **Uttarakhand** is known for its festivals such as **Kumaoni Holi**, **Ganga Dussehra**, and **Harela**, which are deeply tied to its rich cultural and spiritual heritage.
 
• The state is also famous for its **Char Dham Yatra**, an important pilgrimage for Hindus.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh**__
 __
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** celebrates festivals like **Lokrang Festival**, **Khajuraho Dance Festival**, and **Malwa Utsav**, which highlight its diverse cultural traditions and arts.
 
• The state is also home to **tribal festivals**, such as **Bhagoria Festival**, celebrated by the Bhil and Bhilala tribes.
 
 
 
• **Kerala**__
 
 
• **Kerala** is renowned for its iconic festival **Onam**, a harvest festival celebrated with grand feasts, boat races, and cultural programs.
 
• Other notable festivals in Kerala include **Vishu**, **Thrissur Pooram**, and **Theyyam**, which reflect the state's unique cultural identity.

questions.question: Which of the following religions is practiced by most people in China?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Buddhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buddhism** is one of the most widely practiced religions in **China**.
 
• It was introduced to China during the **Han Dynasty** (206 BCE–220 CE) and has since become deeply ingrained in Chinese culture.
 
• There are three main schools of Buddhism in China: **Han Buddhism, Tibetan Buddhism,** and **Theravada Buddhism**.
 
• Key features of Buddhism in China include practices such as **meditation, chanting, and monastic life**.
 
• Numerous historical Buddhist sites in China, such as the **Shaolin Temple** and the **Longmen Grottoes**, are renowned globally.
 
• Many Chinese people also integrate Buddhist principles with elements of **Confucianism** and **Taoism**, forming a unique religious and philosophical blend.
 
• Buddhism emphasizes the concepts of the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path**, which focus on overcoming suffering and attaining enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Islam**__

 __
 
• **Islam** is practiced by a minority in China, primarily by the **Hui**, **Uighur**, and other Muslim ethnic groups.
 
• It was introduced to China during the **Tang Dynasty** via the Silk Road.
 
• Notable Islamic sites in China include the **Great Mosque of Xi'an**, one of the oldest mosques in the country.
 
 
 
• **Christianity**__
 __
 
• **Christianity** is another minority religion in China, having been introduced by missionaries such as **Nestorians** during the Tang Dynasty.
 
• Today, there are two main branches: **Protestantism** and **Catholicism**.
 
• Christianity in China is closely monitored and regulated by the government.
 
 
 
• **Hinduism**__
 
 
• **Hinduism** is not widely practiced in China and has limited historical influence.
 
• However, cultural exchanges between India and China, such as during the **Gupta Dynasty**, introduced certain Hindu concepts to the region.

questions.question: Ramnad V. Raghavan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mridangam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramnad V. Raghavan** was a renowned artist associated with the **Mridangam**, a percussion instrument widely used in Carnatic music.
 
• The **Mridangam** is a double-sided drum made primarily of wood and leather.
 
• This instrument is considered the primary rhythmic accompaniment in **Carnatic music concerts.**
 
• Ramnad V. Raghavan played a significant role in promoting and teaching **Mridangam** both in India and abroad.
 
• He was known for his mastery of rhythm, technique, and his ability to blend traditional and modern styles.
 
• He taught at institutions such as the **Wesleyan University** in the United States, contributing to the global appreciation of Indian classical music.
 
• The **Mridangam** is often played during performances featuring vocalists, violinists, and other Carnatic instrumentalists.
 
• Ramnad V. Raghavan was also known for collaborating with several legendary Carnatic musicians, earning widespread acclaim.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nadaswaram**__

 __
 
• The **Nadaswaram** is a classical wind instrument widely used in South Indian music, particularly in temple rituals and weddings.
 
• It is considered one of the loudest non-brass acoustic instruments in the world.
 
• The Nadaswaram is made of wood and is associated with auspicious occasions.
 
 
 
• **Dholak**__
 __
 
• The **Dholak** is a double-headed drum commonly used in folk music and Bollywood songs.
 
• It is smaller and more portable compared to the Mridangam.
 
• The Dholak is widely used in North Indian music traditions and in devotional gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**__
 
 
• The **Sarangi** is a bowed string instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is known for its ability to mimic the human voice and is often used as an accompaniment to vocal performances.
 
• The Sarangi is made primarily of wood and has gut strings.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts constituted the State Finance Commission?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**73rd Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1992** was a landmark amendment that introduced **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** in India.
 
• This amendment added a new part, **Part IX**, to the Constitution and inserted **Articles 243 to 243O**.
 
• It mandated the establishment of the **State Finance Commission** to ensure the distribution of financial resources between the state and Panchayati Raj Institutions.
 
• The **State Finance Commission** is constituted every **five years** by the state government as per Article **243I**.
 
• The commission is responsible for recommending the principles for the distribution of funds, grants, and financial resources between the **state government** and **local self-governing bodies**.
 
• The amendment aimed to strengthen grassroots-level democracy and ensure financial autonomy for local bodies.
 
• The **73rd Amendment Act** is applicable to all states except, **Nagaland**, **Meghalaya**, and **Mizoram**, as well as certain areas covered under the **Sixth Schedule**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **74th Amendment Act**__

 __
 
• The **74th Constitutional Amendment Act** introduced provisions for **Urban Local Bodies** (Municipalities).
 
• This amendment added **Part IXA** to the Constitution and inserted Articles **243P to 243ZG**.
 
• It aimed to strengthen urban governance by establishing municipalities and ensuring their financial and administrative autonomy.
 
• It mandated the creation of the **District Planning Committees** and **Metropolitan Planning Committees** for integrated planning at the district and metropolitan levels.
 
 
 
• **75th Amendment Act**__
 __
 
• The **75th Amendment Act** deals with enabling provisions for the establishment of **Rent Control Tribunals**.
 
• The act aimed to streamline the process of rent regulation and dispute resolution in urban areas.
 
• It provided states with the power to establish tribunals for speedy adjudication of rent-related disputes.
 
 
 
• **76th Amendment Act**__
 
 
• The **76th Amendment Act** included the **Tamil Nadu Reservation Act** of 1994 in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• This amendment ensured that the reservation policy of Tamil Nadu, which provides **69% reservation** for backward classes, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes, remains protected from judicial review.
 
• The Ninth Schedule was created to shield certain laws from being challenged for violating fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which is the best Indian state for farming in 2024, as per the 15th Agriculture Leadership Awards Committee?

__
 
• **Maharashtra** was recognized as the best Indian state for farming in **2024** by the **15th Agriculture Leadership Awards Committee**.
 
• The state has shown remarkable progress in **agricultural innovation**, adopting modern technologies like **drip irrigation**, precision farming, and sustainable agricultural practices.
 
• **Maharashtra** is a leader in the production of several crops, including **sugarcane, cotton, soybeans, and horticultural crops** such as **grapes, oranges, and pomegranates**.
 
• The state has implemented several **government schemes** and programs, such as the **Jalyukt Shivar Abhiyan**, to improve water conservation and irrigation facilities.
 
• It has a strong network of **Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs)** and agricultural universities like the **Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth**, which focus on **research and development**.
 
• The state’s **agro-climatic diversity** allows the cultivation of a variety of crops, enhancing its agricultural potential.
 
• **Maharashtra** has also focused on **export-oriented agriculture**, particularly in the horticulture sector, boosting the state's economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Punjab**__

 __
 
• **Punjab** is known as the **‘Granary of India’** due to its high agricultural output, especially in **wheat and rice**.

• However, challenges like **depleting groundwater levels** and **soil degradation** have impacted its long-term agricultural sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Haryana**__
 __
 
• **Haryana** is another agricultural powerhouse, known for its contribution to the **Green Revolution**.
 
• The state excels in **wheat, rice, and dairy production**, but it faces issues like **water scarcity** and **environmental concerns**.

• **Gujarat** is famous for its **white revolution** and is a leading producer of **milk and dairy products**.
 
• The state has also achieved success in **horticulture** and **cash crops** like cotton and groundnuts.
 
• However, it is limited in terms of **arable land** compared to states like Maharashtra.

questions.question: The region of the Earth's atmosphere where weather events occur is known as the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Troposphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **troposphere** is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere and extends from the Earth's surface up to an average height of about **8–15 km**, depending on the latitude and season.
 
• This layer contains approximately **75% of the atmosphere's mass** and nearly all of its **water vapor**, making it crucial for weather phenomena.
 
• Weather events such as **rain, snow, storms, and winds** occur in the troposphere due to the presence of water vapor and temperature variations.
 
• The temperature in the troposphere generally decreases with altitude, at an average rate of **6.5°C per kilometer** (known as the lapse rate).
 
• The boundary between the troposphere and the stratosphere is known as the **tropopause**, which acts as a barrier preventing the mixing of air between the two layers.
 
• This layer also plays an important role in the **Earth’s climate system**, as it contains the greenhouse gases that regulate surface temperatures.
 
• The troposphere is where human activities such as aviation and pollution primarily occur, influencing its composition and dynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mesosphere**__

 __
 
• The **mesosphere** is the third layer of the atmosphere, located above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere.
 
• It extends from about **50 to 85 km** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It is the coldest atmospheric layer, with temperatures dropping as low as **-90°C**.
 
• This layer is where **meteors burn up** upon entering the Earth's atmosphere, creating shooting stars.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**__
 __
 
• The **stratosphere** lies above the troposphere and extends from about **15 to 50 km** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It contains the **ozone layer**, which absorbs and scatters ultraviolet solar radiation, protecting life on Earth.
 
• In contrast to the troposphere, the temperature in the stratosphere **increases with altitude** due to the absorption of UV radiation by ozone.
 
• This layer is also relatively stable, making it suitable for **commercial aviation**.
 
 
 
• **Exosphere**__
 
 
• The **exosphere** is the outermost layer of the atmosphere, extending from about **500 km** above the Earth's surface to the edge of space.
 
• This layer contains very few air molecules and is where **satellites orbit**.
 
• The particles in the exosphere can escape into space due to the **low gravity pull** at these altitudes.
